answer: Behavioral cohort clustering. Collect each identity’s interaction graph and timing, then flag correlated activity—shared counterparties, synchronized joins, near-identical transaction cadence—that exceeds chance. A fleet of purportedly independent agents begins to appear as one marble, its members’ histories too smooth and synchronized to be separate. Enforcement delays settlement: flagged cohorts face a copper penalty on aggregate volume, and suspicious clusters lose routing priority at the shared jetty where payouts clear.
